note: Slide-deck annotation taxonomy. Narrative Style (pick one), Content Style (select all), Visual Style (sub-dimensions shown together: Background pick one, Layout select all, Content Presentation pick one) and Textual Style (select all). Flags: `single` = at most one concept selectable; `group`/`tab` = categories sharing a group id render together. Longer per-concept explanations (shown under each category) live in `desc`.

categories.label: Narrative Style
categories.desc: How information is organized and developed across the deck. Pick the single dominant structure.

concepts.label: Source-based
concepts.desc: Organized around individual source documents, with each source presented largely as a separate unit. e.g. Paper A → Paper B → Paper C

concepts.label: Topic-based
concepts.desc: Organized around topics, themes, or concepts, potentially combining information from multiple sources within each topic. e.g. Architectures → Applications → Challenges

concepts.label: Time-based
concepts.desc: Organized around the chronological development of events, ideas, or technologies. e.g. Early developments → Recent advances → Future directions

concepts.label: Step-by-step
concepts.desc: Follows an ordered sequence of processes, stages, or learning dependencies, where each section builds on the preceding one. e.g. Data collection → Processing → Training → Evaluation

concepts.label: Comparison-based
concepts.desc: Organized around systematic comparisons of approaches, alternatives, or entities across different dimensions. e.g. Accuracy → Efficiency → Limitations comparison

concepts.label: Reasoning-based
concepts.desc: Develops a central question, problem, or claim through a sequence of explanations, evidence, and conclusions. e.g. Problem → Existing limitations → Evidence → Proposed solution

categories.label: Content Style
categories.desc: How information from multiple source documents is presented, connected, and synthesized. Select all that apply.

concepts.label: Independent
concepts.desc: Presents contributions, methods, or findings from multiple sources without establishing substantial connections between them.

concepts.label: Comparative
concepts.desc: Explicitly compares contributions from multiple sources to identify similarities, differences, relative strengths, or trade-offs.

concepts.label: Shared Limitations
concepts.desc: Identifies common weaknesses, unresolved challenges, or research gaps across multiple source documents.

concepts.label: New Directions
concepts.desc: Builds on contributions from multiple sources to propose future research directions, new approaches, hypotheses, or potential improvements.

concepts.label: Insights
concepts.desc: Combines findings from multiple sources to establish shared principles, complementary relationships, unified explanations, or broader conclusions.

categories.label: Background Style
categories.desc: The background appearance of the slides.

concepts.label: Plain White/Dark
concepts.desc: Slides primarily use near-white or dark-colored backgrounds with minimal decoration.

concepts.label: Colored or Graphic
concepts.desc: Slides use prominent colors, gradients, patterns, images, or graphical backgrounds.

concepts.label: Mixed
concepts.desc: The deck combines different background styles across slides.

categories.label: Layout Style
categories.desc: The spatial arrangement of content on the slides. Select all that apply.

concepts.label: Title and Body
concepts.desc: Slides follow a conventional layout with a title at the top and a main content area underneath.

concepts.label: Split Bodies
concepts.desc: Slides divide content into two or more distinct regions, commonly arranged side by side or vertically.

concepts.label: Multiple Grid-Based Panels
concepts.desc: Slides organize content into multiple structured panels or blocks arranged in a grid-like layout.

concepts.label: Visual-Focused
concepts.desc: Slides are dominated by a central figure, image, chart, or diagram, with supporting text playing a secondary role.

categories.label: Content Presentation
categories.desc: The balance between textual and visual content on the slides.

concepts.label: Text-Focused
concepts.desc: Information is predominantly communicated through text, with visuals playing a supporting role.

concepts.label: Balanced
concepts.desc: Information is presented through a relatively equal combination of text and visual elements.

concepts.label: Visual-Focused
concepts.desc: Information is predominantly communicated through figures, images, diagrams, or other visuals, with minimal supporting text.

categories.label: Textual Style
categories.desc: The dominant text format on the slides. Select all that apply.

concepts.label: Paragraph-based
concepts.desc: The deck primarily presents information through continuous prose, with multiple sentences grouped into paragraphs or extended text blocks.

concepts.label: Bullet-based
concepts.desc: The deck primarily presents information through bulleted or numbered lists, with each point communicating a separate idea or supporting detail.

concepts.label: Sentence-based
concepts.desc: The deck primarily uses short, standalone sentences or statements, typically occupying one or two lines without forming paragraphs or lists.

concepts.label: Short-phrase-based
concepts.desc: The deck primarily uses short phrases, keywords, labels, or brief callouts rather than complete sentences or extended explanations.

concepts.label: Question–Answer-based
concepts.desc: The deck frequently presents information through explicit questions and corresponding answers, with questions serving as the main textual framing of the slides.
